title: The dispatcher runs without a session sitting open
description:
`runQueue` in packages/core/src/queue.ts:29 already does the dispatching: it takes every node that is ready and whose brief was approved with `queue: true` (ADR 0017), skips one another person has claimed, skips one heading for the same files as another in the wave, and hands the rest to `dispatchWave` — which is where the concurrency limit and the stop-at-the-first-failure rule already live. None of that needs building.

What is missing is stated in that file's own doc comment: "There is no daemon and no watcher." The only caller is `drain` in packages/cli/src/queue.ts, and `drain` is reached from exactly two places — packages/cli/src/work.ts:178 after an accept, and packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts:360 after a decision is answered. So a node becomes ready and starts only if a human happened to be in the session that moved the graph. A run that finishes at 02:00, a teammate's accept arriving through `sync`, a decision answered in another clone — none of those start anything. The queue is correct and mostly idle.

Build the long-lived half: a process that drains on a cycle instead of on an event. It calls the same `runQueue`, so every safety rule in ADR 0017 is inherited rather than reimplemented — do not fork the logic. It must hold or respect the writer lock from ADR 0025 (`lock.staleSeconds`, `lock.waitSeconds` in .sober/config.jsonc), because a drainer that writes while a human's `accept` writes is exactly what that lock exists to stop. It must also be safe to start twice: the second one finds the first and says so rather than doubling every dispatch.

What it does NOT do, and why this is worth saying in the code: it does not dispatch a ready node whose brief carries no `queue: true`. ADR 0017 lists "Dispatch every ready node automatically" under its rejected alternatives — "Removes D26's approval, which is the last thing a human sees before an agent starts working" — and the charter says nothing runs without a human-approved brief. The user asked for every ready node; that is one predicate in `queued()` away, and it is deliberately not taken here. If it is wanted, it is an ADR superseding 0017, not a line changed quietly.

Acceptance: with the dispatcher running and nobody in any session, approving a node with queue and then accepting its last dependency starts it within one cycle; starting a second dispatcher refuses and names the first; stopping it leaves running agents in a state `sober status` reports honestly. Tests beside the code, with the cycle driven rather than slept through.

brief.approach:
Score 6: the dispatching logic already exists and must not be forked — the work is a loop, a lock, and two rules that are easy to state and easy to get wrong.

**What exists and is not rebuilt.** `runQueue` in `packages/core/src/queue.ts:29` takes every node that is ready and approved with `queue: true` (ADR 0017), skips one another person has claimed, skips one heading for the same files as another in the wave, and hands the rest to `dispatchWave`, where concurrency and the stop-at-the-first-failure rule already live. `drain` in `packages/cli/src/queue.ts` already renders its result — what started, what finished, what is held and why. Call both. A second copy of any of that logic is the failure this node is most likely to produce.

**The command.** `sober dispatch` in `packages/cli/src/index.ts` — a new case beside `dashboard`, a new row in the help under **Build**, and the implementation beside `drain` in `packages/cli/src/queue.ts`. Foreground, Ctrl-C stops it: the accepted decision chose the shape `sober dashboard` already has ("serve the board in a browser — Ctrl-C stops it and its runs"), so the user has met it before. Print one line on start saying it is draining on `<base>` and that Ctrl-C stops it, then loop: `drain(paths, base)`, wait, repeat. A cycle that starts nothing prints nothing — a dispatcher that logs every idle tick is one nobody leaves running.

The interval is a config key beside the other dispatch settings in `packages/core/src/config.ts` (schema, `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, and the commented `DEFAULT_CONFIG_TEXT` block — all three, they are one file and one edit). Something like `dispatch.pollSeconds`, defaulting to a value in the tens of seconds, with a comment saying what it costs: a file read per tick, and a node waits at most that long after becoming ready.

**Two rules, both load-bearing.**

1. **Safe to start twice.** The second one finds the first and says so rather than doubling every dispatch. The writer lock from ADR 0025 (`withLock` in `packages/core/src/lock.ts`, windows from `lock.staleSeconds` / `lock.waitSeconds`) is the mechanism — it is also what stops the drainer writing while a human's `accept` writes, which is what the lock exists for. The accepted decision's cost line is explicit that there is no way to ask "is one running" from another shell, so the twice-started case has to be caught through the lock rather than a pid file: hold it (or take it each cycle) and let the second process report that another one holds it, naming the holder the way `withLock` already names it. Do **not** add a pidfile — the decision rejected on-disk liveness precisely because it goes stale.

2. **A failure stops the drain entirely.** ADR 0017 already decided this for one drain — a queued chain stops at the first rejection or failure, so four more nodes are never built on a result a human turned down. A loop that carried on next cycle would quietly convert "stop" into "stop until the next tick", which is not stopping. So when a cycle reports a failed dispatch, print what failed and **exit the loop**, non-zero, with the sentence that says a human has to look. The queue stopping is the loudest signal an unattended process has.

**What it deliberately does not do**, and this belongs in a comment in the code, not only in the brief: it does not dispatch a ready node whose brief carries no `queue: true`. ADR 0017 lists "Dispatch every ready node automatically" under its rejected alternatives — it removes the approval, which is the last thing a human sees before an agent starts working — and the charter says nothing runs without a human-approved brief. It is one predicate in `queued()` away and is deliberately not taken. If it is ever wanted, it is an ADR superseding 0017, not a quiet line change.

**Tests** in `packages/cli/src/queue.test.ts` (create it if it is not there) and one integration case in `test/integration/queue.test.ts`, which already drives the queue end to end. Drive the cycle, never sleep through it: factor the loop so the wait is an injectable function or the loop body is a callable `tick`, and call it directly. Three cases: a node approved with queue that becomes ready between two ticks is started by the second; a tick whose dispatch fails ends the loop non-zero and says so; a second dispatcher started while the first holds the lock refuses and names it.

Nothing in `packages/mcp`, `packages/server` or `apps/dashboard` changes. Watching the dispatcher is `watching-the-dispatcher-what-it-started-9skj`, which waits on this node.

acceptance.proves: the loop starts a node that became ready between ticks, ends non-zero on a failed dispatch instead of carrying on next cycle, and a second dispatcher refuses while the first holds the writer lock
the queue's existing rules still hold through the new command: an unapproved brief is not started, a claimed node is left to its owner, and an overlapping node is never started unattended

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'runQueue' -- packages/cli/src/queue.ts && test -z "$(git diff --name-only development -- packages/core/src/queue.ts)"
acceptance.proves: the dispatching logic was called, not forked — core's queue is untouched and every ADR 0017 safety rule is inherited rather than reimplemented

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'pollSeconds' -- packages/core/src/config.ts && test "$(git grep -c 'pollSeconds' -- packages/core/src/config.ts)" != 'packages/core/src/config.ts:1'
acceptance.proves: the interval is a real config key — in the schema, in DEFAULT_CONFIG and in the commented template a person actually reads
liveness is the writer lock and not a file on disk — the accepted decision rejected on-disk liveness because it goes stale

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'dispatch' -- packages/cli/src/index.ts && pnpm vitest run --project integration test/integration/cli.test.ts -t 'help'
acceptance.proves: the command is wired and appears in `sober --help`, so it is findable without reading the source

acceptance.run: test -z "$(git diff --name-only development -- packages/mcp packages/server apps)"
acceptance.proves: no other surface changed: watching the dispatcher is a separate node that waits on this one
the new command and the widened config compile across the monorepo
